CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for reassessment of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, headache symptoms, and medication side effects.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, stating that he has experienced a slight improvement in his overall symptoms since the last visit. He reports that the reduction of amitriptyline to 5 mg nightly has significantly decreased his daytime sedation, allowing him to feel more alert and engaged during the day. However, he notes that while his tension-type headaches have remained stable at approximately 2 to 3 episodes per week, the intensity of these headaches has not diminished, leading him to use ibuprofen more frequently.
Sleep quality remains suboptimal; Mr. Smith continues to average about 5 hours of sleep per night, with frequent awakenings. He has been adhering to cognitive-behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) techniques but finds it challenging to implement due to ongoing work-related stress. He reports that his anxiety levels have fluctuated, with increased feelings of restlessness and worry, particularly as project deadlines approach at work.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 100 mg daily 2. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief 5. Amitriptyline 5 mg nightly
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer and reports maintaining his walking routine three times a week. He expresses satisfaction with his stretching exercises, which he finds beneficial for both physical and mental well-being. He has further reduced his alcohol intake, attending social gatherings with minimal consumption. Additionally, he remains committed to mindfulness meditation and has begun incorporating breathing exercises to help manage acute anxiety episodes.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Reports ongoing anxiety, persistent sleep disturbances, improved daytime alertness, no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms noted. - Neurological: Tension-type headaches as described, no visual changes or focal neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. - General: Persistent fatigue, no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 122/78 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, no motor or sensory deficits. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative, maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with ongoing anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline 100 mg daily; consider an adjustment in therapy if anxiety symptoms persist or worsen. Discuss the option of adding a short-term anxiolytic if acute anxiety episodes increase. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin 3 mg at bedtime; reinforce CBT-I strategies and sleep hygiene practices. Monitor the effects of the reduced amitriptyline on both sleep and headache management. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen 400 mg as needed; assess headache frequency and intensity at the next visit to determine if further prophylactic treatment is necessary. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage ongoing physical activity and mindfulness practices; consider evaluating for potential underlying sleep disorders if fatigue persists despite medication adjustments.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2027-03-01 to further evaluate symptoms, treatment effectiveness, and medication side effects. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or side effects from medications.
